Founded and directed by EV Voltura, PhD.

fits.s: Began with one person's question, why macaws eat clay, carried from a childhood in Alaska to a PhD.
fits.p: Undergraduates do real research: 39 students built a 2,188-record dataset on what cockatoos eat.
fits.u: Gathers parrot names across languages and scripts, verified by native speakers and credited on their terms.
fits.o: Keeps a public reference library and public knowledge graphs, every record traced to its source.
fits.h: Joins science, veterinary care, aviculture, conservation and history in one connected library.

nodes.name: Drifting Through Deep Time
nodes.summary: Follows Earth's surface through time: where the continents sat, what grew on them, how the climate shifted, and who walked across them.
nodes.keywords: deep time geology plate tectonics paleoclimate pollen vegetation human migration archaeology ancient dna linguistics myth oral history ecology conservation climate policy geoscience education philosophy of time

fits.s: Asks what it feels like to stand on rock 400 million years old.
fits.p: Students build and check the visualizations, and elders review the module.
fits.u: Joins geology, ecology, archaeology, linguistics, myth and oral history around one question: what did this place look like?
fits.o: Built on open plate-reconstruction and public climate datasets, and shared openly.
fits.h: The example hub of the Open Commons: core layers and bordering fields that other labs can join.

hubs.note: Know how you learn, what you believe, and where your gaps are. “Know thyself” was carved at the temple of Apollo at Delphi, and Socrates made it the starting point of philosophy.

Theory and action together: learn by doing real work, then reflect on it. Aristotle set praxis, thoughtful action, beside theory. Paulo Freire defined it as reflection and action upon the world in order to transform it.
Knowledge open to everyone, and fields connected into a whole. The word university comes from the Latin universitas: the whole community of teachers and scholars.
Knowledge free to read and reuse: open articles, open data, open courses and open tools, so that anyone can learn and build on what is known.
Shared hubs where labs, schools and communities in one field work together and connect across fields, joined into one network.
Continents, vegetation, climate, and human migration layered across 540 million years. The first hub in this network.

A living library that gathers what people have recorded about parrots (scientific papers, veterinary case reports, avicultural journals, photographs, theses, citizen-science observations) and connects it while keeping every record's source and context. Founded and directed by EV Voltura, PhD (Texas A&M). Its work includes knowledge graphs, a history of parrot names since 1758, multilingual species names, a student-built cockatoo diet dataset, and a hyperspectral feather library. A participating node of The Open Commons of Learning.
